items.question: A car travels at 60 km per hour. How far does it go in 3 hours?
items.explanation: Distance = Speed × Time. So 60 × 3 = 180 km. Each hour the car covers 60 km, and 3 hours gives 180 km.

items.question: There are 3,600 seconds in one hour.
items.explanation: One minute has 60 seconds and one hour has 60 minutes. So one hour has 60 × 60 = 3,600 seconds.

items.question: A train covers 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
items.explanation: Step 1: 2 hours 30 minutes = 2.5 hours. Step 2: Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 km/h.

items.question: 36 km per hour is the same as ___ metres per second.
items.explanation: 1 km = 1,000 m and 1 hour = 3,600 seconds. So 36 km/h = 36,000 m ÷ 3,600 s = 10 m/s. Shortcut: multiply km/h by 5/18 (36 × 5 ÷ 18 = 10).

items.question: You walk to a shop at 4 km/h and walk back the same way at 6 km/h. What is your average speed for the whole trip?
items.explanation: Say the shop is 12 km away (easy to divide). Going takes 12 ÷ 4 = 3 hours, coming back takes 12 ÷ 6 = 2 hours. Total: 24 km in 5 hours, so 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 km/h. It is not 5, because you spend more time at the slower speed.
